title: Geometry & Mensuration
intro: Geometry is the largest single block in SSC Tier 2, so the payoff for mastering it is huge. It splits into pure geometry (angles, triangle and circle theorems, centres) and mensuration (areas and volumes). The winning habit is to memorise the standard results — angle sums, similarity ratios, the area and volume formulas — and to draw a clean figure for every question. This chapter equips you with the formula sheet and the theorem reflexes SSC tests again and again.

items.name: Area of triangle
items.formula: (1/2) x base x height; Heron: root(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c))

items.name: Exterior angle
items.formula: equals sum of opposite interior angles

items.name: Circle
items.formula: area = pi r^2, circumference = 2 pi r

items.name: Cuboid volume / Cube
items.formula: l x b x h ; a^3

items.name: Cylinder
items.formula: volume pi r^2 h, curved surface 2 pi r h

topics.name: Lines & Angles
topics.details: When two lines meet, vertically opposite angles are equal and a linear pair sums to 180 degrees. With a transversal across parallel lines, corresponding and alternate angles are equal and co-interior angles sum to 180. Angles around a point sum to 360. These rules, plus the triangle angle sum, settle most figure-chasing questions.

solved.problem: Two angles are complementary and one is 35 degrees. The other?
Two angles on a straight line; one is 110 degrees. The other?
Parallel lines cut by a transversal; one alternate angle is 65 degrees. Its pair?
Three angles around a point are 120, 150 and x. Find x.

topics.name: Triangles & Congruence
topics.details: A triangle's angles sum to 180; an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles. Pythagoras holds in right triangles. Similar triangles have equal angles and proportional sides; if the side ratio is k, the area ratio is k^2. Standard centres: the centroid divides each median 2:1. Memorise common Pythagorean triples (3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17) for instant answers.

solved.problem: Two angles of a triangle are 50 and 60 degrees. The third?
Right triangle legs 6 and 8. Hypotenuse?
Similar triangles have side ratio 2:3. Area ratio?
Exterior angle of a triangle is 120, one remote interior is 50. The other remote?

unsolved.problem: Centroid divides a median in ratio?
hints: Vertex to centroid : centroid to midpoint.

topics.name: Circles
topics.details: Key circle theorems: the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc; the angle in a semicircle is 90 degrees; equal chords are equidistant from the centre; the tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact; and tangents drawn from an external point are equal. Cyclic-quadrilateral opposite angles sum to 180.

solved.problem: Angle at centre is 80 degrees on an arc. Angle at circumference?
Angle in a semicircle?
A cyclic quadrilateral has one angle 95 degrees. Its opposite angle?
A tangent meets a radius at the point of contact. The angle between them?

unsolved.problem: Two tangents from an external point compare how?

topics.name: 2D Mensuration
topics.details: Master the plane-figure formulas: rectangle lb, square a^2, triangle (1/2)bh (or Heron's for three sides), parallelogram base x height, trapezium (1/2)(sum of parallel sides) x height, circle pi r^2 with circumference 2 pi r. Use pi = 22/7 when the radius is a multiple of 7. For a path/border, subtract the inner area from the outer.

solved.problem: Area of a rectangle 12 by 8?
Area of a circle of radius 7 (pi = 22/7)?
Area of a triangle base 10, height 6?
Area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 and 12, height 5?

unsolved.problem: Area of a square of side 9?

topics.name: 3D Mensuration
topics.details: Solid formulas: cuboid volume lbh (surface 2(lb+bh+hl)); cube a^3 (surface 6a^2); cylinder pi r^2 h (curved surface 2 pi r h); cone (1/3) pi r^2 h (slant l = root(r^2+h^2)); sphere (4/3) pi r^3 (surface 4 pi r^2); hemisphere (2/3) pi r^3. When a solid is melted and recast, volume is conserved — equate the two volumes.

solved.problem: Volume of a cuboid 5 x 4 x 3?
Volume of a cube of side 6?
Volume of a cylinder r = 7, h = 10 (pi 22/7)?
A sphere r = 3 is melted into a cylinder of radius 3. Find the cylinder height.
solved.solution: Sphere vol = (4/3) pi 27 = 36 pi; cylinder pi 9 h = 36 pi -> h = 4.

shortcuts: Exterior angle = sum of remote interior angles.
Use pi = 22/7 when the radius is a multiple of 7.
Recast/melt problems: volume is conserved — equate volumes.
mistakes: Using side ratio instead of its square for area ratio.
Confusing curved surface with total surface area.
Mixing radius and diameter in circle formulas.
pyq: SSC Tier 2 packs in circle theorems, triangle centres/similarity, and recast mensuration (sphere to cylinder/cone). Draw the figure and label every known value first.

flashcards.q: Area ratio of similar triangles, sides 2:3?

summary: Lock in angle rules, triangle and circle theorems, and the full area/volume formula sheet. Use similarity (area = side^2 ratio), pi = 22/7 for multiples of 7, and volume conservation for recast solids. Always draw and label the figure.
